key_insight: NeuronSoup uses asynchronous, delay-mediated signal propagation through shared neurons to evolve temporal computation without backpropagation.
engineering_relevance: It suggests a compact, non-differentiable alternative for classification systems where adaptive computation depth and pathway interactions matter.
method: Encode the whole network as a 14,602-gene real-valued genome.
Evolve topology, weights, delays, and connectivity with a genetic algorithm.
Reuse hidden neurons across paths so arrival order and signal polarity create interference effects.
evidence_signal: On frozen ResNet18 features for 10-class MNIST, the evolved model used 204 active paths, 266 hidden neurons, and reached 85.9% test accuracy after 10,000 generations with a 115 KB model size.
watch_item: Because performance depends on large-scale evolutionary search and asynchronous state interactions, training cost, reproducibility, and deployment timing behavior may be difficult to control.
paper_title: NeuronSoup: Evolving Asynchronous, Shared-Neuron Temporal Graphs without Backpropagation
